page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is a storage-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Lasv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 vector extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography (AES, VAES, SHA_NI).

This instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes a bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark evaluations, the L8as_v4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core performance, database operations, and memory write bandwidth fall within the average range. However, uncached read memory bandwidth for large blocks (256 MB) and prompt processing for medium-sized LLM models (7B) represent performance bottlenecks, placing in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L8as_v4 offers a high local NVMe storage-to-compute ratio and dense memory allocation, making it a viable option for workloads requiring fast local scratch space without the overhead of external storage arrays. The server is well-suited for database operations, text processing, web serving, and general-purpose workloads that benefit from high single-core speed and local NVMe storage, though it is less optimal for memory-intensive uncached read operations or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is an x86_64 storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores), 64.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supports AVX-512 extensions and hardware cryptography. Benchmark data highlights strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, while multi-core execution, database operations, and memory write bandwidth remain average. A notable performance tradeoff is its weak uncached large-block read memory bandwidth. Qualitatively, the server provides high local storage density relative to its compute resources. It is best suited for database workloads, text processing, and web serving applications requiring fast local NVMe storage.
